chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Abu al-Jawza', from al-Husayn, from Amr ibn Khalid, from Zayd ibn Ali, from his fathers, from Ali (peace be upon him).

Regarding a man who publicly declared the divorce of his wife and witnessed it, but kept his revocation (raj'ah) secret; then he left, and when he returned he found that she had married another. He said: 'He has no right over her because he kept his revocation secret and made her divorce public.'

key_terms.أَشْهَدَ: He witnessed / He made it witnessed
key_terms.أَظْهَرَ: He made public / He declared openly
key_terms.رَجْعَة: Revocation (of divorce by the husband during the waiting period)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a husband's right to revoke divorce if he publicly announced it but secretly performed the revocation?
ai.summary: This narration from Zayd ibn Ali highlights the jurisprudential principle that public declaration (zuhur) takes precedence over secret action (sir) in marital status, a key distinction in Shia fiqh regarding the finality of divorce. It illustrates how the husband's concealment of the revocation while the public witnessed the divorce renders the revocation ineffective, thereby preventing him from reclaiming her without a new contract. This ruling underscores the importance of transparency in legal acts to protect the wife's rights and ensure social clarity.
